packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (packet-04). Images only; no outside source consulted; no identification of work or author attempted.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- 18 images. image-001 = overview of side A; image-002..009 = reading-size pieces of side A; image-010 = overview of side B; image-011..018 = pieces of side B.
- One parchment leaf (or the lower/upper part of one), upright, written in TWO columns on both sides, roughly 49-50 lines per column visible. The top line of each column begins mid-sentence, so text is lost above (trimmed) or continues from another leaf; a wide blank lower margin survives on both sides.
- A horizontal fold/abrasion band crosses both columns about 6-8 lines from the bottom, with two small holes; the lines in that band are badly rubbed, especially on side A.
- No running titles, no rubrics, no colour. Paragraph marks (pilcrow-shaped, in the text ink) open new items inside the lines. One larger pen-flourished initial on side B right column (a long descending stroke before "albedo", image-016 line 7). No underlining apart from a later underline beneath a catchword-like word at the foot of side B.
- Margins: side A outer left margin has a pencil numeral/mark "1"(?) at top and an ink sign shaped like "H"/"ff" beside line 4-5; side B right margin has a modern pencil note written vertically (looks like "Fragm. lat. 32 a"?, not relied on), two ink "H"-like marginal signs (image-016 beside line 5; image-018 top right) and a red crayon mark "4"(?) (image-016). No interlinear gloss.
- Foot of side B right column: a word written apart below the last line, underlined, "idens"(?) - placed where a catchword would be; it appears to complete the divided word "respo(n)-" of the last line (so possibly just the run-over of the last word).
- Script: small, compact, very heavily abbreviated book hand in brown ink; the sign "÷" stands throughout for a word (est), "7" for et, a g with superscript o for ergo, "So." for a proper name, an "H"-like capital with superscript a opening many sentences (expansion uncertain; rendered Ia~? below).
- Tentative interpretation only: a run of short self-contained argument units, each opened by a pilcrow and an example sentence, followed by chains of "ergo ... ergo ..." and a closing remark such as "quod falsum est". No visible separation into main text and commentary.

AREAS SELECTED
Side A: top of left column (image-002), top of right column (image-003), middle of right column (image-005, part).
Side B: top of left column (image-011, 013), top and middle of right column (image-012, 014, 016), foot of right column (image-018).
UNREAD OR ONLY SAMPLED: side A left column middle and bottom (image-004, 006, 008), side A right column lower half (image-007, 009); side B left column lower half (image-015, 017). The fold band on side A is largely illegible in these images.

Conventions: (..) proposed expansion; ? uncertain; [illegible]; ÷ kept as written (the "est" sign); 7 = Tironian et; ¶ = paragraph mark.
